name: Cdo

subjectOf.text: Because rating agencies are paid by CDO issuers while the ratings' main users are buyers, the agency as agent has an incentive to issue high ratings to satisfy its issuer principal, and the buyer has no means of controlling the agency other than through its relationship with the issuer.
subjectOf.abstract: The rating agency as the agent would probably have an incentive to issue high ratings to satisfy the issuer of a CDO as its principal. The buyer as the beneficiary of the rating has no means of controlling the rating agencies and its ratings other than through its relationship with the issuer.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, Hedge Fund Valuation Retailization, Regulation, and Investor Suitability (2009). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=1428387
scope_conditions: under the issuer-pays model for structured finance ratings

subjectOf.text: The issuer-buyer relationship and the incentives inside it are unlikely to be able to adequately control the principal-agent relationship between issuer and rating agency so as to ensure accurate ratings.
subjectOf.abstract: It seems unlikely that the issuer-buyer relationship and the incentives inherent within could adequately control the principal-agent relationship between issuer and rating agency to ensure accurate ratings.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, Hedge Fund Valuation Retailization, Regulation, and Investor Suitability (2009). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=1428387
scope_conditions: under the issuer-pays rating model for CDOs

subjectOf.text: Market failure in complex financial instruments, rather than hedge fund activity as such, could have been a contributing factor in the recent credit crisis.
subjectOf.abstract: Market failure in complex financial instruments could have been a contributing factor in the recent credit crisis.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, Hedge Fund Regulation Via Basel III (2011). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=1806252
scope_conditions: evidence drawn from the 2007 collapse of the CDO and CDS markets

subjectOf.text: Although hedge funds manage only a small proportion of the investment universe compared with banks, they do manage a proportionally large part of complex financial instruments such as CDOs and other derivatives.
subjectOf.abstract: However, it appears that hedge funds do manage a proportionally large part of complex financial instruments, such as CDOs and other derivatives.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, Hedge Fund Regulation Via Basel III (2011). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=1806252
